title: The Excise-Fiscal Diagnostic
subtitle: Reading an excise system against its externalities
message: A light, repeatable report maps any excise schedule onto 30 standard lines, scales each rate three ways and sets fuel rates against one fixed set of damage values. Run on Sierra Leone and Liberia in 2026, it finds excise at 1.3 and 0.4 percent of GDP against an African average of 2.4.

problem.text: Schedules grow by amendment for decades, in mixed units and currencies, and specific rates erode with inflation. Few ministries can say whether a fuel, tobacco or alcohol tax is high or low against the damage the good does.

mechanism.title: Two countries, two different gaps
mechanism.caption: Excise-Fiscal Diagnostic, 2026 runs; illustrative results, not official estimates.
points: Sierra Leone: about 90% of excise from fuel, on a large base at $0.23 per liter.
Liberia: fuel pays $0.095 in levies, below the carbon cost alone.
Both: health excises legislated, weakly collected; Liberia books no tobacco excise on imports.

action.title: Run it every budget cycle
results: Spirits pay less per liter of alcohol than beer in Liberia, as in the stylized case.
Sierra Leone's 2024 switch to leone rates cut beer and wine rates by about 70% or more in dollars.
Stylized case: diesel at less than half its corrective rate; air pollution, not carbon, is the gap.
